files.mmogr/gglib/.github/workflows/ci.yml@21a:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

# A pull request's runs share one group, and a newer run cancels the older:
# after a force-push or an `@dependabot rebase` the older run is testing a
# commit nobody will merge.
#
# A push to main gets a group of its own, named by its SHA, so no other CI
# run ever joins it. GitHub keeps at most one run pending in a group and
# cancels the older pending run when a newer one arrives, whatever
# `cancel-in-progress` says, so one group shared by main's pushes would drop
# runs merged in quick succession, and the push run is the one that runs
# `release`, which tags. The builds it dispatches run in release.yml under
# a group of the tag's own, out of this workflow's reach.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('ci-pr-{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) || format('ci-main-{0}', github.sha) }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Read only. A job that needs more says so: `scope`, `cache-prune` and
# `release`.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

# Every job has a timeout-minutes, counted from when it starts rather than
# from when it was queued: a ceiling for a hang, well above a cold run. The
# cross-OS legs take theirs from the matrix: 75 minutes on macOS, where CLI
# Check builds llama.xcframework when its cache misses, and 45 elsewhere.
jobs:
  fmt:
    name: Format
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup show

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

  quality:
    name: Lint & Typecheck
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: '.nvmrc'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # The design-system guardrails in eslint.config.js (the raw <button> ban,
      # the emoji ban, the @tauri-apps import boundary) were advisory until this
      # job existed — nothing in CI ran eslint. --max-warnings 0 also keeps
      # react-hooks/exhaustive-deps from accumulating silently.
      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint -- --max-warnings 0

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

  # No `needs:` — nothing here compiles the workspace, so gating these behind
  # `fmt` only lengthened the critical path. `ci-success` still requires every
  # job, so nothing loses enforcement.
  #
  # This job and `enforcement` below run the Makefile targets
  # `make pre-commit` runs and name no check of their own, so CI and a local
  # run cannot check different things.
  boundaries:
    name: Check Boundaries
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Check crate boundaries
        run: make boundaries

      # A dependency a manifest declares and none of that crate's targets
      # names. cargo-shear reads the source as text and compiles nothing, so
      # code for another platform or behind a feature counts as a use.
      - name: Install cargo-shear
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@68a389c788b2cd04016ce8c80ee23b80d2ab3d68 # v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-shear

      - name: Check for unused dependencies
        run: make unused-deps

      - name: Upload boundary results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with:
          name: boundary-results
          path: boundary-status.json

  enforcement:
    name: Enforce Architecture
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # check_workflow_yaml.sh runs it and fails here without it. The release
      # tarball, checked against the checksum its release lists, so a moved
      # asset cannot change what lints. shellcheck comes with the runner.
      - name: Install actionlint
        env:
          URL: https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/releases/download/v1.7.12/actionlint_1.7.12_linux_amd64.tar.gz
          SHA256: 8aca8db96f1b94770f1b0d72b6dddcb1ebb8123cb3712530b08cc387b349a3d8
        run: |
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint.tar.gz" "$URL"
          echo "$SHA256  $RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint.tar.gz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP" actionlint
          sudo install "$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint" /usr/local/bin/actionlint
          actionlint --version
          shellcheck --version

      # Every architecture script, in the order the Makefile's `enforce` recipe
      # lists them. The first to fail ends the step, and its output is the end
      # of the log. Among them is the workflow YAML check, which cannot catch a
      # break in this file: GitHub starts no job from a workflow it will not
      # parse, so `make pre-commit` is where that case is caught, before the
      # push.
      - name: Run the architecture checks
        run: make enforce

  # Each reading an ADR's criterion names, in contracts/upstream/llama's
  # observed.json, against its hand-kept approval. It reads two committed
  # files and never starts an engine, so a recorder that fails cannot turn it
  # red; a reading that moved, or one nobody has approved, does.
  adr-readings:
    name: ADR criterion moved
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Check each ADR reading against its approval
        run: make adr-readings

  test:
    name: Test (Rust)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # No `needs:`. This was chained to `clippy` so it would restore the target
    # dir clippy had just populated — but clippy builds `--all-features` and
    # this job builds default features, so on run 32705784511 it inherited
    # 2.57 GB and got 49 of 630 units fresh. Five minutes of serialization for
    # a cache that was 92% inapplicable. Each job has its own shared-key now,
    # so each warms from its own history instead of the other's.
    #
    # Every test step below pipes into `tee` so the output survives as an
    # artifact, and a pipeline reports its *last* command's status — `tee`'s,
    # which is always 0. GitHub's default shell is `bash -e` without pipefail,
    # so a failing `cargo test` was reported as a passing step: three of the
    # six CI runs before this change were green with a failing test inside.
    # `shell: bash` is `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`, which makes
    # cargo's status the one that counts.
    #
    # Set per job rather than on the workflow: a workflow-level default would
    # also reach `cli-cross-os`, which runs on windows-2022, and switching that
    # leg from pwsh to Git Bash has nothing to do with this problem.
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # A shared-key per build configuration, and only main saves; the
      # rust-prelude action says why. `large-packages` stays off because this
      # job installs the GTK and appindicator packages it would purge.
      - name: Rust prelude
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust-prelude
        with:
          apt-packages: >-
            libgtk-3-dev
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev
            librsvg2-dev
            libasound2-dev
          shared-key: "ci-test"
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Lockfile guard
        run: cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 > /dev/null

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: '.nvmrc'
          cache: 'npm'

      # gglib-axum embeds `web_ui/` and its tests serve `/` from it.
      - name: Build Web UI
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      # One build, then one run over it. The fifteen-crate loop this replaces
      # cost 23m15s of a 57m job, and it was not merely repeating work: naming
      # a crate with `-p` changes feature unification, so `cargo test -p
      # gglib-runtime` ran 329 tests where the workspace build ran 352. The 23
      # in llama::{build,config,deps,download,update} sat behind features
      # gglib-cli turned on, so the loop tested a configuration no real build
      # used and the badge was 23 tests short of the truth.
      #
      # `--no-run` first for two reasons: a compile failure stays
      # distinguishable from a test failure, and the JSON is where the
      # binary-to-package map comes from. It cannot come from the text —
      # `integration_guards` belongs to gglib-agent and says so nowhere.
      - name: Build test binaries
        run: cargo test --no-run --message-format=json > cargo-test-artifacts.json

      # `--no-fail-fast` is a deliberate change, not a transcription. Without
      # it cargo stops at the first failing binary, so on a red run every later
      # crate's tests go unrun and the log says nothing about them. One failure
      # should not hide the state of everything after it.
      #
      # No `--verbose`: nothing parses the per-rustc lines and they were 5324
      # of this step's log. And no `--all-targets`, ever — it would silently
      # drop the doctests, which this step is the only thing running now that
      # the separate `cargo test --doc` step is gone. split_test_output.py
      # fails a green run that produced no Doc-tests sections, which is the
      # standing guard for that.
      - name: Run Rust tests
        run: cargo test --no-fail-fast 2>&1 | tee rust-test-output.txt

      # The download accelerator's helper is Python, so `cargo test` does not
      # run it. Its tests drive its progress bar through the huggingface_hub
      # the requirements file pins. In a venv, so nothing is installed into
      # the runner's own Python.
      - name: Test the download helper
        run: |
          python3 -m venv /tmp/hfx
          /tmp/hfx/bin/pip install --quiet -r crates/gglib-download/scripts/hf_xet_requirements.txt
          cd crates/gglib-download/scripts && /tmp/hfx/bin/python -m unittest test_hf_xet_downloader

      # badges.yml counts per-crate tests out of rust-test-<crate>.txt,
      # through scripts/write_badges.py. Those used to come from the loop
      # above; they now come from dividing the one run's output by the package
      # each binary belongs to. `always()` so a red suite still publishes what
      # it did run.
      - name: Split test output per crate
        if: always()
        run: ./scripts/split_test_output.py cargo-test-artifacts.json rust-test-output.txt

      - name: Upload test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with:
          name: test-results
          # A glob, so the set is whatever the run built.
          path: rust-test-*.txt
          retention-days: 30

  bindings:
    name: Bindings Freshness
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Its own job rather than a step on `test`, which is where it lived on the
    # stated grounds that "the cargo cache is warm in this job". It was not:
    # this builds `--features ts-bindings`, a different feature unification
    # from the one `test` had just produced, and the log shows it recompiling
    # accordingly. Three minutes seventeen of critical path buying nothing that
    # a job running in parallel does not buy for free.
    #
    # The frontend's wire types are generated from the Rust types, and the
    # generated output is committed so the GUI build needs no cargo. That only
    # stays honest if something regenerates and compares — otherwise a changed
    # Rust field ships against a stale TypeScript mirror, which is the whole
    # class of drift the generation exists to end.
    #
    # Staleness only. The annotations themselves are checked by
    # `check_ts_bindings.sh` in `enforcement`, because a missing annotation
    # regenerates consistently and leaves this diff clean.
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Its own shared-key, and only main saves; the rust-prelude action
      # says why.
      - name: Rust prelude
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust-prelude
        with:
          apt-packages: >-
            libgtk-3-dev
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev
            librsvg2-dev
            libasound2-dev
          shared-key: "ci-bindings"
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      # No frontend build. gglib-axum compiles without `web_ui/`: the
      # `#[allow_missing = true]` in its `src/ui.rs` leaves the embedded asset
      # set empty. The one member whose build can need it is gglib-app, whose
      # `tauri::generate_context!()` embeds `frontendDist` when its
      # `custom-protocol` feature is on, and `make bindings` excludes it.
      - name: Check generated TypeScript bindings are current
        run: make bindings-check

  rustdoc:
    name: Rustdoc
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # Off `test` for the same reason as `bindings` above: it sat there for a
    # cargo cache that did not apply to it. rustdoc builds its own artifacts
    # and the job log shows 137 crates recompiling, so the four and a half
    # minutes it took were four and a half minutes of critical path.
    #
    # The same invocation release.yml's `deploy-docs` publishes with, run on
    # every PR so a broken link is caught by the change that breaks it rather
    # than by whoever next cuts a release: `deploy-docs` runs only for a
    # release, so nothing else checks rustdoc on the way in.
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Its own shared-key, and only main saves; the rust-prelude action
      # says why.
      - name: Rust prelude
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust-prelude
        with:
          apt-packages: >-
            libgtk-3-dev
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev
            librsvg2-dev
            libasound2-dev
          shared-key: "ci-rustdoc"
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      # No frontend build. gglib-axum compiles without `web_ui/`: the
      # `#[allow_missing = true]` in its `src/ui.rs` leaves the embedded asset
      # set empty. The one member whose build can need it is gglib-app, whose
      # `tauri::generate_context!()` embeds `frontendDist` when its
      # `custom-protocol` feature is on, and `--exclude gglib-app` leaves it out.
      - name: Check rustdoc has no warnings
        env:
          RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings
        run: ./scripts/doc_workspace.py -- --document-private-items --exclude gglib-app

      # rustdoc does not warn about a Markdown link that goes nowhere, and a
      # crate README is its front page, so a relative link that works on
      # GitHub can break here with the step above green.
      - name: Check the links on each crate's front page
        run: python3 scripts/check_doc_links.py target/doc

  test-frontend:
    name: Test (Frontend)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # No `needs:` — this job is pure npm and finishes in about a minute. It used
    # to wait on a full workspace clippy build it shares nothing with.
    # Same masking as the Rust job: `npm run test:run … | tee` reported `tee`'s
    # exit status, so a failing suite passed the step. See the note there.
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: '.nvmrc'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # Two orphan barrels sat in `src/` because nothing looks for files that
      # nothing imports: `tsc` is happy to compile an island, and eslint only
      # ever sees one file at a time. Scoped to files, dependencies and
      # unlisted imports — the export-level classes are noisier and are not
      # gated yet, deliberately. `npm run deadcode` is the same command.
      - name: Check for dead files and undeclared dependencies
        run: npm run deadcode

      - name: Run TypeScript tests
        run: npm run test:run -- --reporter=json --reporter=default --outputFile=ts-test-results.json 2>&1 | tee ts-test-output.txt

      - name: Upload test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with:
          name: ts-test-results
          path: |
            ts-test-output.txt
            ts-test-results.json
          retention-days: 30

  clippy:
    name: Clippy
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # No `needs:` — clippy is a long pole and nothing gates it. It no longer
    # warms anyone else's cache: it builds `--all-features`, which is not what
    # `test` or `cli-cross-os` build, and the shared key that pretended
    # otherwise cost `test` five minutes of waiting for artifacts it could not
    # use.
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Its own shared-key, and only main saves; the rust-prelude action
      # says why.
      - name: Rust prelude
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust-prelude
        with:
          apt-packages: >-
            libgtk-3-dev
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev
            librsvg2-dev
            libasound2-dev
          shared-key: "ci-clippy"
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: '.nvmrc'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Build Web UI
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      - name: Run clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

  cli-cross-os:
    name: CLI Check (${{ matrix.target }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.timeout }}
    # Only when `scope` says a change can reach these builds. `clippy` first,
    # so no macOS or Windows minutes go on a tree ubuntu clippy has rejected.
    if: needs.scope.outputs.cross_os == 'true'
    needs: [clippy, scope]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            timeout: 45
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-26
            timeout: 75
          - target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
            os: windows-2022
            timeout: 45
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Its own shared-key per target, and only main saves; the rust-prelude
      # action says why. Main runs this job when Cargo.lock or the toolchain
      # moves, so the key the next pull requests restore is saved there. The
      # Linux leg builds one crate and needs no disk freed.
      - name: Rust prelude
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust-prelude
        with:
          free-disk: "false"
          apt-packages: libasound2-dev
          shared-key: "ci-cli-${{ matrix.target }}"
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Check gglib-cli compilation
        run: cargo test -p gglib-cli --no-run

      # The pinned engines themselves, on the two platforms whose builds a
      # runner can run. The `gglib` just built installs each one as a user's
      # machine would, into a folder of the job's own, and the action fetches
      # the recorder's tiny models; both are cached. Each engine's `--help`
      # and each pinned release's asset list then go to `gglib-runtime`'s
      # ignored tests: every flag and fixed value gglib starts an engine with
      # must be one its `--help` lists, and every row of the two download
      # tables must match exactly one asset. `--version`, which gglib also
      # runs both servers with, is run here directly: sd-server's `--help`
      # does not list it.
      - name: Install the pinned engines and the test models
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        id: engines
        uses: ./.github/actions/pinned-engines
        with:
          target: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Save the engines' help and the releases' assets
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ENGINES: ${{ steps.engines.outputs.engines }}
        run: |
          help="$RUNNER_TEMP/engine-help"
          assets="$RUNNER_TEMP/engine-assets"
          mkdir -p "$help" "$assets"
          "$ENGINES/.llama/bin/llama-server" --help > "$help/llama-server.txt" 2>&1
          "$ENGINES/.llama/bin/llama-bench" --help > "$help/llama-bench.txt" 2>&1
          "$ENGINES/.sd/bin/sd-server" --help > "$help/sd-server.txt" 2>&1
          "$ENGINES/.llama/bin/llama-server" --version
          "$ENGINES/.sd/bin/sd-server" --version
          gh release view "${{ steps.engines.outputs.llama }}" -R ggml-org/llama.cpp \
            --json assets -q '.assets[].name' > "$assets/llama.txt"
          gh release view "${{ steps.engines.outputs.sd }}" -R leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp \
            --json assets -q '.assets[].name' > "$assets/sd.txt"

      - name: Check every flag gglib passes is one the pinned engines take
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        env:
          GGLIB_ENGINE_HELP_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/engine-help
          GGLIB_ENGINE_ASSETS_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/engine-assets
        run: cargo test -p gglib-runtime --lib -- --ignored

      # The pinned llama-server, started through gglib's own launch path on
      # the tiny models, writes what it answered into contracts/upstream
      # (engine_contract_tests.rs says what is kept). Report-only for now, as
      # is the comparison below: a recorder or a reading that is not yet
      # stable on a runner shows in the step summary without blocking a merge.
      # The models variable is set on this step alone, so the ignored tests
      # above skip the recorder.
      - name: Record the pinned llama-server
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        id: record
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GGLIB_ENGINES_DIR: ${{ steps.engines.outputs.engines }}
          GGLIB_ENGINE_MODELS_DIR: ${{ steps.engines.outputs.models }}
          GGLIB_ENGINE_BODIES_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/upstream-bodies
          GGLIB_RECORD_CONTRACTS: "1"
        run: cargo test -p gglib-runtime --lib engine_contract -- --ignored --nocapture

      - name: Compare with contracts/upstream
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          PIN: ${{ steps.engines.outputs.llama }}
          ARTIFACT: ${{ runner.os == 'Linux' && 'upstream-recordings' || format('upstream-recordings-{0}', matrix.target) }}
          RECORDED: ${{ steps.record.outcome }}
        run: |
          if [[ $RECORDED != success ]]; then
            echo "::error title=the recorder did not finish::Read the \"Record the pinned llama-server\" step on ${{ matrix.target }}; contracts/upstream was not checked."
            echo "The recorder did not finish on ${{ matrix.target }}, so contracts/upstream was not checked." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 1
          fi
          changed=$(git status --porcelain -- contracts/upstream | awk '{print $2}')
          if [[ -z $changed ]]; then
            echo "contracts/upstream matches what $PIN answered on ${{ matrix.target }}." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi
          names=$(xargs -n1 basename <<<"$changed" | paste -sd, - | sed 's/,/, /g')
          count=$(wc -l <<<"$changed" | tr -d ' ')
          echo "::error title=contracts/upstream is stale::$count files differ from what $PIN answered on this tree: $names. Run \`make record-upstream\` on this branch, or download artifact \`$ARTIFACT\` from this run and commit it."
          {
            echo "### contracts/upstream on ${{ matrix.target }}: $count files differ from what $PIN answered"
            echo
            echo '```diff'
            git diff -- contracts/upstream | head -c 60000
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          exit 1

      # The in-process engine, a phone's: gglib-engine-llama over llama.cpp's
      # own llama.xcframework at the pin, asked the same questions on the same
      # models, into contracts/upstream/llama-inproc (engine_contract_inproc.rs
      # says what differs). macOS only, where the framework builds, and
      # report-only as the llama-server recording is: a framework that does
      # not build, a recorder that fails or a recording that moved shows in the
      # step summary. Test (Rust) holds the committed recording to llama's on
      # every OS. The flag that turns the recorder on is set on its step alone.
      - name: Build or restore llama.xcframework at the pin
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        id: xcframework
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: ./.github/actions/llama-xcframework

      - name: Record the in-process engine
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && steps.xcframework.outcome == 'success'
        id: record-inproc
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GGLIB_ENGINE_MODELS_DIR: ${{ steps.engines.outputs.models }}
          GGLIB_INPROC_ENGINE: "1"
          GGLIB_RECORD_CONTRACTS: "1"
        run: >-
          cargo test -p gglib-runtime --lib --features inproc-contract
          engine_contract_tests::the_in_process_engine -- --ignored --nocapture

      - name: Compare with contracts/upstream/llama-inproc
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          PIN: ${{ steps.engines.outputs.llama }}
          BUILT: ${{ steps.xcframework.outcome }}
          RECORDED: ${{ steps.record-inproc.outcome }}
        run: |
          if [[ $BUILT != success || $RECORDED != success ]]; then
            echo "::error title=the in-process recorder did not finish::Read the \"Build or restore llama.xcframework at the pin\" and \"Record the in-process engine\" steps; contracts/upstream/llama-inproc was not checked."
            echo "The in-process recorder did not finish, so contracts/upstream/llama-inproc was not checked." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 1
          fi
          changed=$(git status --porcelain -- contracts/upstream/llama-inproc | awk '{print $2}')
          if [[ -z $changed ]]; then
            echo "contracts/upstream/llama-inproc matches what the in-process engine answered at $PIN." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi
          names=$(xargs -n1 basename <<<"$changed" | paste -sd, - | sed 's/,/, /g')
          count=$(wc -l <<<"$changed" | tr -d ' ')
          echo "::error title=contracts/upstream/llama-inproc is stale::$count files differ from what the in-process engine answered at $PIN on this tree: $names. Run \`make record-upstream-inproc\` on a Mac on this branch, or download artifact \`upstream-recordings-${{ matrix.target }}\` from this run and commit its llama-inproc/."
          {
            echo "### contracts/upstream/llama-inproc: $count files differ from what the in-process engine answered at $PIN"
            echo
            echo '```diff'
            git diff -- contracts/upstream/llama-inproc | head -c 60000
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          exit 1

      - name: Gather the recordings
        if: runner.os != 'Windows' && always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          out="$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-recordings"
          mkdir -p "$out"
          cp -R contracts/upstream/. "$out/"
          if [[ -d $RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-bodies ]]; then
            rm -rf "$out/llama/bodies"
            cp -R "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-bodies" "$out/llama/bodies"
          fi

      # The artifact is laid out as contracts/upstream is, with the redacted
      # bodies in llama/bodies/, so committing it is unpacking it there.
      - name: Upload the recordings
        if: runner.os != 'Windows' && always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ runner.os == 'Linux' && 'upstream-recordings' || format('upstream-recordings-{0}', matrix.target) }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/upstream-recordings
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # The `clippy` job above runs on ubuntu only, so until now no lint had ever
  # seen the inside of a `#[cfg(windows)]` block. `cli-cross-os` visits all
  # three platforms but only compiles — `cargo test --no-run` does not lint.
  #
  # Running it turned up four kinds of thing in code that had been there for
  # months: an import unused on Windows, an unreadable literal, enum variants
  # dead on Windows, and a function that could be `const` there.
  #
  # Linux is deliberately absent: the `clippy` job already covers it with the
  # same invocation, and repeating it here would only spend runner minutes.
  #
  # Whole workspace rather than the crates that carry `#[cfg]`. Two reasons:
  # a hand-kept crate list goes stale the first time someone adds platform
  # code to a crate not on it, and — measured while writing this — naming a
  # subset changes feature unification, flipping rustls off `ring` and onto
  # `aws-lc-sys`, which then wants a C toolchain. The whole workspace is both
  # the honest scope and the one that builds. It needs the Web UI for the same
  # reason the `clippy` job does: `gglib-app` embeds it.
  clippy-cross-os:
    name: Clippy (${{ matrix.target }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.timeout }}
    # As `cli-cross-os`: when `scope` says so, and after ubuntu clippy.
    if: needs.scope.outputs.cross_os == 'true'
    needs: [clippy, scope]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-26
            timeout: 75
          - target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
            os: windows-2022
            timeout: 45
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Its own shared-key per target, and only main saves, as for
      # `cli-cross-os`.
      - name: Rust prelude
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust-prelude
        with:
          shared-key: "ci-clippy-${{ matrix.target }}"
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: '.nvmrc'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Build Web UI
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      - name: Run clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

  # The crates a phone build compiles, the Makefile's PHONE_CRATES, checked
  # for aarch64-apple-ios. On macOS because ring, aws-lc-sys and the bundled
  # SQLite compile C for the target in their build scripts, which takes
  # Xcode's iOS SDK. That the same crates reach no desktop-only package is the
  # `boundaries` job's: it reads their closure for this target from the
  # metadata, with no Apple toolchain.
  #
  # Whenever `scope` says a change reaches a Rust build. It waits for `scope`
  # alone, not `clippy`, so an iOS break shows without the longest job ahead
  # of it.
  ios-check:
    name: iOS Check
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 45
    needs: [scope]
    if: needs.scope.outputs.ios == 'true'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # rust-toolchain.toml lists the Apple targets, so the toolchain step
      # installs them. Its own shared-key, and only main saves; the
      # rust-prelude action says why.
      - name: Rust prelude
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust-prelude
        with:
          shared-key: "ci-ios-check"
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Check the phone crates for aarch64-apple-ios
        run: make ios-check

  # What a change can reach, read once on Linux so the macOS and Windows jobs
  # run only when it can matter to them. scripts/ci_scope.py says what each
  # output means; every gated job's `if:` and `ci-success` read these and
  # nothing else.
  #
  # A pull request is the merge commit against its first parent. A push is
  # compared with the commit main was at before it, since one push can carry
  # several commits; `before` is all zeros only when a branch is created, and
  # then the commit's parent stands in. The pull request count is for an
  # admin's direct push, which no pull request CI has seen.
  scope:
    name: Scope
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      version_only: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.version_only }}
      rust: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.rust }}
      ffi: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.ffi }}
      ios: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.ios }}
      lock: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.lock }}
      cross_os: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.cross_os }}
      apple: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.apple }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The head and its parent: a pull request's base, or a push's
          # fallback.
          fetch-depth: 2

      # scripts/apple/ffi-inputs-changed.sh reads gglib-ffi's closure with
      # `cargo tree`.
      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup show

      - name: Decide what this change can reach
        id: scope
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BEFORE: ${{ github.event.before }}
          SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if [[ $EVENT == pull_request ]]; then
            ./scripts/ci_scope.py scope --base HEAD^1 --head HEAD >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          base=HEAD^1
          if [[ ! $BEFORE =~ ^0+$ ]]; then
            git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "$BEFORE"
            base=$BEFORE
          fi
          prs=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$SHA/pulls" --jq length)
          ./scripts/ci_scope.py scope --base "$base" --head "$SHA" --event push --pr-count "$prs" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # gglib-ffi as the app links it: GglibFFI.xcframework, a dynamic framework
  # per slice (iOS device, iOS simulator, macOS) linking llama.cpp's own
  # llama.framework at the pin, checked slice by slice, the committed Swift
  # binding held to what the library generates, and that binding compiled and
  # called against the macOS slice, its served engine streaming a reply from
  # tinygemma3 on the Mac's CPU. It boots no simulator.
  #
  # llama.xcframework comes from the llama-xcframework action, which restores
  # the one `phone-llama` cached for the pin and the runner's Xcode, or builds
  # it; the model comes from the pinned-engines action, as CLI Check's do.
  #
  # The runner's default Xcode, as ggchat's CI uses: the framework this
  # builds is the one an app built with that Xcode links. Unoptimised, since
  # nothing it answers depends on optimisation; release.yml builds the
  # optimised one it ships.
  ffi-apple:
    name: Swift Framework (macOS)
    runs-on: macos-26
    needs: [scope]
    if: needs.scope.outputs.apple == 'true'
    # A cold build of three slices, the generator and the Swift package is a
    # few minutes, and llama.cpp's three builds half an hour more when its
    # cache misses; the ceiling is for a hang, not for a slow runner.
    timeout-minutes: 75
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # rust-toolchain.toml lists the three Apple targets, so the toolchain
      # step installs them. Its own shared-key, and only main saves; the
      # rust-prelude action says why. Main saves it whenever a push reaches
      # the framework.
      - name: Rust prelude
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust-prelude
        with:
          shared-key: "ci-ffi-apple"
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      # After the Rust cache, never before it: rust-cache pre-cleans target/
      # when it restores another Cargo.lock's entry, and that clean deletes
      # every file under target/ outside a profile's own folders, the
      # framework in target/apple included. A version bump is such a run.
      - name: Build or restore llama.xcframework at the pin
        uses: ./.github/actions/llama-xcframework

      - name: Xcode and Swift
        run: |
          xcodebuild -version
          swift --version

      # The pinned-engines action without its engines: the recorder's tiny
      # models, restored, fetched and saved under the key CLI Check uses, and
      # the pin's chat templates beside them.
      - name: Fetch the test models
        id: models
        uses: ./.github/actions/pinned-engines
        with:
          target: aarch64-apple-darwin
          engines: "false"

      - name: Build the XCFramework and check each slice
        run: make ffi-xcframework-fast

      - name: The committed Swift binding is what the library generates
        run: make ffi-binding-check

      - name: The Swift binding links and calls the macOS slice, and its engine streams a reply
        env:
          GGLIB_ENGINE_MODELS_DIR: ${{ steps.models.outputs.models }}
        run: make ffi-smoke

  # llama.cpp's own llama.xcframework at the pin, built by upstream's script
  # with the runner's Xcode for the iPhone, its simulator and the Mac, and
  # checked for the slices and the llama.h functions the phone engine links.
  # The llama-xcframework action caches it by the pin, the Xcode version and
  # the build script, so a run compiles llama.cpp only when one of them moves.
  #
  # Then the phone engine's decoder over llama.h (gglib-engine-llama's `llama`
  # feature) is built against that framework, the one place CI links it: its
  # tests on the Mac's slice, on the CPU, read the tiny models the CLI Check
  # legs record with, and fail if they are missing; clippy lints it for the
  # Mac, the iPhone and its simulator. Every other job builds the crate as
  # plain Rust, with no framework.
  #
  # When the change reaches the Swift framework's inputs, as `ffi-apple`:
  # gglib-engine-llama is in gglib-ffi's closure, and the pin, the
  # llama-xcframework action and the test models' list are inputs. A run that
  # misses the xcframework cache saves its entry, so a pull request restores
  # main's entry or one an earlier run of its own saved.
  phone-llama:
    name: Phone Engine on llama.cpp (macOS)
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 75
    needs: [scope]
    if: needs.scope.outputs.apple == 'true'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # rust-toolchain.toml lists the Apple targets, so the toolchain step
      # installs them. Its own shared-key, and only main saves; the
      # rust-prelude action says why.
      - name: Rust prelude
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust-prelude
        with:
          shared-key: "ci-phone-llama"
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      # After the Rust cache, never before it: rust-cache pre-cleans target/
      # when it restores another Cargo.lock's entry, and that clean deletes
      # every file under target/ outside a profile's own folders, the
      # framework in target/apple included. A version bump is such a run.
      - name: Build or restore llama.xcframework at the pin
        uses: ./.github/actions/llama-xcframework

      # The pinned-engines action without its engines, as `ffi-apple` runs it.
      - name: Fetch the test models
        id: models
        uses: ./.github/actions/pinned-engines
        with:
          target: aarch64-apple-darwin
          engines: "false"

      - name: The decoder over llama.h, tested on the Mac's slice
        env:
          GGLIB_ENGINE_MODELS_DIR: ${{ steps.models.outputs.models }}
        run: make engine-llama-test

      - name: The decoder over llama.h, linted for the Mac, the iPhone and its simulator
        run: make engine-llama-clippy

  # Main's Rust caches, down to the newest entry per job and toolchain.
  # rust-cache keys an entry
  # `v0-rust-<shared-key>-<os>-<arch>-<env hash>-<lockfile hash>` and
  # restores by everything before the lockfile hash, so once a newer entry
  # exists for the same job and env hash an older one is never restored
  # again; but it stays until the repository's 10 GB limit evicts something,
  # and what it evicts first is the macOS entries, saved least often. Every
  # lockfile change leaves a generation of these behind, so this runs on
  # every push. The env hash stays in the group: two runner images with
  # different toolchains serve the pool at once during a rollout, and each
  # restores only its own lineage.
  #
  # After the jobs that save on most pushes, so their new entries are
  # counted; an entry the macOS jobs save later is pruned by the next push.
  cache-prune:
    name: Prune the Rust caches
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: [test, bindings, rustdoc, clippy, cli-cross-os, clippy-cross-os]
    permissions:
      actions: write
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # A failure here costs cache space, not correctness, and must not turn
      # main's run red: the release pull request and the badges follow only
      # a green one. A delete that loses a race with another run's prune is
      # a warning.
      - name: Delete every entry but the newest per job and toolchain
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          gh cache list --ref refs/heads/main --json id,key,createdAt --limit 500 \
            | jq -r '[.[] | select(.key | test("^v0-rust-.+-[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{8}$"))]
                     | group_by(.key | sub("-[0-9a-f]{8}$"; ""))
                     | .[] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[:-1][] | "\(.id) \(.key)"' \
            > "$RUNNER_TEMP/stale.txt"
          echo "$(wc -l < "$RUNNER_TEMP/stale.txt") stale entries"
          while read -r id key; do
            echo "Deleting $key"
            gh cache delete "$id" < /dev/null || echo "::warning::could not delete $key"
          done < "$RUNNER_TEMP/stale.txt"

  # The one required check. A gated job's own `if:` reads its scope output,
  # and this holds every job to what that output says it must have done:
  #
  #   job                            must be
  #   cli-cross-os, clippy-cross-os  success if cross_os, else skipped
  #   ios-check                      success if ios, else skipped
  #   ffi-apple, phone-llama         success if apple, else skipped
  #   every other job                success
  #
  # A skip is a pass only where its gate says `false`, so a gate that comes
  # out wrong, or empty because `scope` failed, cannot turn a run green with
  # the job unrun. A matrix job reports one result for all its legs.
  ci-success:
    name: CI Success
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: always()
    needs: [scope, boundaries, bindings, enforcement, adr-readings, quality, rustdoc, test, test-frontend, clippy, clippy-cross-os, fmt, cli-cross-os, ios-check, ffi-apple, phone-llama]
    steps:
      - name: Check every job did what its scope says
        env:
          NEEDS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        shell: python3 {0}
        run: |
          import json, os, sys

          GATES = {
              "cli-cross-os": "cross_os",
              "clippy-cross-os": "cross_os",
              "ios-check": "ios",
              "ffi-apple": "apple",
              "phone-llama": "apple",
          }
          OUTPUTS = ("version_only", "rust", "ffi", "ios", "lock", "cross_os", "apple")

          needs = json.loads(os.environ["NEEDS"])
          scope = needs.get("scope", {}).get("outputs", {})
          bad = []
          for name in OUTPUTS:
              value = scope.get(name)
              print(f"scope: {name}={value}")
              if value not in ("true", "false"):
                  bad.append(f"scope output {name} is {value!r}, not true or false")
          for job in GATES:
              if job not in needs:
                  bad.append(f"{job} is gated here but missing from needs")
          for job, info in sorted(needs.items()):
              gate = GATES.get(job)
              want = "success" if gate is None or scope.get(gate) == "true" else "skipped"
              got = info["result"]
              print(f"{job}: {got}" + (f" ({gate}={scope.get(gate)})" if gate else ""))
              if got != want:
                  bad.append(f"{job} is {got}, and must be {want}")
          for line in bad:
              print(f"::error::{line}")
          sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

  release:
    name: Release
    needs: [ci-success]
    if: always() && needs.ci-success.result == 'success' && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    # A called workflow cannot exceed the caller's grant: these are exactly
    # what release-tag.yml's create-release job asks for. The two secrets
    # are the App's, which makes the tag; nothing else is passed.
    permissions:
      contents: write
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
      actions: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/release-tag.yml
    secrets:
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
files.mmogr/gglib/.github/workflows/release-ta:
# The tagging half of a release, called by ci.yml's `release` job after CI
# passes on a push to main, so its check shows on the commit. When main's
# version has no `v<version>` tag it tags the commit that set that version,
# makes the GitHub (pre)release, and dispatches release.yml, which builds and
# publishes the assets in a run of its own. Nothing that cancels this CI run
# can then cancel the builds.
#
# This tags every candidate. release-please.yml never tags, and promote.yml
# tags a stable version itself, from the candidate's tag, so a promotion
# never comes this way.
#
# Run by hand, it tags without waiting for CI: the same steps on main as it
# is now, and then the release PR workflow, which otherwise follows CI. That
# is the maintainer's shortcut past a CI run that takes an hour, taken on
# their own judgement of the tree: nothing here has tested it. A CI run that
# finishes afterwards finds the tag and releases nothing twice.

name: Release tag

on:
  workflow_call:
    secrets:
      APP_ID:
        required: true
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY:
        required: true
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    # GitHub's default is `bash -e`; this adds pipefail.
    shell: bash

jobs:
  check-version:
    name: Check Version Change
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.version.outputs.changed }}
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      is-prerelease: ${{ steps.version.outputs.is-prerelease }}
      bump: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The whole history and every tag: the bump commit is found in the
          # history, and a stable version is compared with its last RC's tag.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Get current version
        id: version
        run: |
          VERSION=$(grep -m1 '^version = ' Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/version = "(.*)"/\1/')
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # A prerelease is any version carrying a -alpha, -beta or -rc suffix.
          if [[ "$VERSION" == *"-alpha"* ]] || [[ "$VERSION" == *"-beta"* ]] || [[ "$VERSION" == *"-rc"* ]]; then
            echo "is-prerelease=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "is-prerelease=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

          # Asked of the remote rather than the checkout's tags, so a tag made
          # since the checkout counts.
          if git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/v${VERSION}" > /dev/null; then
            echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "v$VERSION is already tagged"
          else
            echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "New version detected: v$VERSION"
          fi

      # The tag goes on the commit that set the version, not on this run's
      # commit. When runs overlap, or a run is cancelled and a later one picks
      # the version up, the run that tags can be testing a newer commit; the
      # bump commit is the same whichever run gets there.
      #
      # -G matches a line the commit added or removed. The newest such commit
      # is the one that added it, since main still carries the line.
      - name: Find the commit that set the version
        id: bump
        if: steps.version.outputs.changed == 'true'
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          ver_re=$(printf '%s' "$VERSION" | sed 's/[.[\*^$/]/\\&/g')
          bump=$(git log -1 --format=%H -G"^version = \"${ver_re}\"\$" -- Cargo.toml)
          if [ -z "$bump" ]; then
            echo "::error::no commit in main's history sets version = \"$VERSION\" in Cargo.toml"
            exit 1
          fi
          git show "$bump:Cargo.toml" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/bump-Cargo.toml"
          if [ "$(grep -m1 '^version = ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/bump-Cargo.toml")" != "version = \"$VERSION\"" ]; then
            echo "::error::$bump was found as the commit that set $VERSION, but its Cargo.toml says otherwise"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "sha=$bump" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "v$VERSION will tag $bump"

      # A stable version is released only as its last release candidate with
      # the version changed. promote.yml makes one that way from the
      # candidate's tag and never comes here, so this guards a version set
      # to stable on main by hand. Checked before anything is tagged, so a
      # refusal leaves no tag and no release behind; the script's header
      # says how to recover. Judged on the bump commit's own tree, so a bump
      # whose run was overtaken is not judged on a newer one.
      - name: Require a stable release to match its last RC
        if: steps.version.outputs.changed == 'true' && steps.version.outputs.is-prerelease != 'true'
        env:
          BUMP: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          git checkout --detach "$BUMP"
          scripts/check_rc_promotion.sh

  create-release:
    name: Create Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    needs: check-version
    if: needs.check-version.outputs.changed == 'true'
    permissions:
      # The tag and the release.
      contents: write
      # The release PR's labels, below: the issues list finds it, and a
      # label on a pull request needs pull-requests: write even through the
      # issues endpoints (issues: write alone got a 403 on v0.29.0-rc.4).
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
      # The dispatch of release.yml.
      actions: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      VERSION: ${{ needs.check-version.outputs.version }}
      BUMP: ${{ needs.check-version.outputs.bump }}
    steps:
      # Through the API, which creates the tag only if no tag of that name
      # exists. Two overlapping runs on main can both find the version
      # untagged; the one that loses gets a 422 and stops here, and the
      # winner makes the release and dispatches the build.
      #
      # A re-run of this job after it failed past this step meets its own
      # tag, on the bump commit, and carries on: the release is made if it
      # is missing, and the build dispatched again (a second dispatch waits
      # in release.yml's concurrency group, then replaces the assets as a
      # whole). The attempt number is what tells that from a lost race,
      # where the loser is on its first attempt and the winner's release
      # may not exist yet.
      # The tag is made with the App's token. GITHUB_TOKEN may create a
      # ref only at the run's own commit: at any other it gets a 403 with
      # `X-Accepted-Github-Permissions: contents=write,workflows=write`, a
      # permission it never has. The bump commit is the run's own only when
      # nothing merged after the release PR before this ran, which a hand
      # run or a busy main breaks. The App has that permission (its
      # settings: "Workflows: read and write").
      - name: App token
        id: app
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Tag the bump commit
        id: tag
        env:
          ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
        run: |
          if out=$(gh api -X POST "repos/$GH_REPO/git/refs" -f ref="refs/tags/v$VERSION" -f sha="$BUMP" 2>&1); then
            echo "tagged=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Tagged $BUMP as v$VERSION"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "$out"
          # A 422 also answers a bad sha, so only an existing tag counts.
          if ! grep -q 'HTTP 422' <<< "$out"; then exit 1; fi
          at=$(gh api "repos/$GH_REPO/git/ref/tags/v$VERSION" --jq .object.sha) || exit 1
          if [ "$at" = "$BUMP" ] && [ "$ATTEMPT" -gt 1 ]; then
            echo "tagged=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::v$VERSION is already on $BUMP from an earlier attempt of this run; carrying on from there"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "tagged=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "::notice::another run tagged v$VERSION; this run makes no release and dispatches nothing"

      # The notes are generated, sorted by .github/release.yml.
      - name: Create GitHub Release
        if: steps.tag.outputs.tagged == 'true'
        env:
          PRERELEASE: ${{ needs.check-version.outputs.is-prerelease }}
        run: |
          if gh release view "v$VERSION" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "the release for v$VERSION exists already"
            exit 0
          fi
          args=(--title "Release v$VERSION" --generate-notes --verify-tag)
          if [ "$PRERELEASE" = "true" ]; then args+=(--prerelease); fi
          gh release create "v$VERSION" "${args[@]}"

      # From main, whose release.yml is the current one; it checks out the tag.
      # A failed build is re-run with the same command.
      - name: Dispatch the build
        if: steps.tag.outputs.tagged == 'true'
        run: gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f tag="v$VERSION"

      # release-please.yml never tags (it runs with skip-github-release), so it
      # cannot see that the release PR it opened has been released, and it
      # opens no other while a merged release PR is labelled
      # `autorelease: pending`. Swapping that label for `autorelease: tagged`
      # is how a release tells it. Only the merged PR titled for this version
      # is touched; a promotion has no such PR, and nothing changes. Last and
      # allowed to fail, so a label can never hold up the build: if it fails,
      # release-please.yml stops with an error naming the label.
      - name: Mark the release PR as tagged
        if: steps.tag.outputs.tagged == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/github-script@v9
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = `chore(main): release ${process.env.VERSION}`;
            // The issues list rather than search, which can lag behind a label.
            const items = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listForRepo, {
              owner, repo, state: 'closed', labels: 'autorelease: pending', per_page: 100,
            });
            for (const item of items) {
              if (!item.pull_request?.merged_at || item.title !== title) continue;
              await github.rest.issues.removeLabel({
                owner, repo, issue_number: item.number, name: 'autorelease: pending',
              });
              await github.rest.issues.addLabels({
                owner, repo, issue_number: item.number, labels: ['autorelease: tagged'],
              });
              core.info(`#${item.number} is now labelled autorelease: tagged`);
            }

      # Run by hand there is no CI run for release-please.yml to follow, so
      # it is started here, after the relabel above: its gate reads that
      # label.
      - name: Refresh the release PR
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && steps.tag.outputs.tagged == 'true'
        run: gh workflow run release-please.yml --ref main
